synopsis: Chapter 7 identifies Wilson intervals, alongside exact-binomial intervals, as methods provided by NIST for situations where normal approximations fail, including small samples and probabilities near 0 or 1 [f5450]. Chapter 9 describes Wilson intervals as less conservative than Clopper-Pearson and better behaved at moderate sample sizes [f6893]. The glossary retains Clopper-Pearson as the conservative default when misses occur, while naming Wilson as a less conservative alternative at moderate sample sizes [f14211]. The supplied facts give no numerical sample-size threshold for choosing Wilson over Clopper-Pearson [f5450, f6893, f14211].

relations.note: Wilson’s comparative behavior supports its recommendation as a less conservative alternative.
Adds NIST provenance and situations where normal approximations fail.
